answer: Common-neighbor scarcity scoring resists sybils: an edge is trusted in proportion to how many INDEPENDENT already-trusted identities both endpoints share, so a fresh fake with no genuine mutual connections scores near zero however many edges it draws. A cedar-walled cluster on its own terrace shares neighbors only with itself; the prism of real trust refracts only through overlapping honest relationships. An attacker cannot fabricate shared trusted neighbors it was never connected to, so sybil edges carry no weight.
